name: paper-figures
title: Executable Figures
lead: This investigation makes the meta-modeler's guide's own figures runnable. Where `draft-to-living-cell` takes the paper's composition patterns to calibrated, spatially-resolved rigor, this one takes the ELEVEN PUBLISHED FIGURES and shows that each panel-b bigraph diagram is a real composition that executes its caption's principle. Panels a (the BioRender illustrations) and the rendered b-panel diagrams are unchanged — this investigation adds the executable substance behind them: one runnable composite per figure, each behind a behavior gate that asserts the figure's claim on real simulation output. Fig 1's process moves a conserved quantity between wired stores; Fig 4's cell senses a diffusing nutrient gradient and drifts up it; Fig 5's grain selector flips coarse→fine as viability crosses its bound, biomass growing then decaying; Fig 9 divides one cell into two with stores partitioned; Fig 11's population evolves toward a shifting selection optimum. Figures fig-03 through fig-11 cross-link a rigorous spatially-resolved cousin in `draft-to-living-cell` via `parent_studies`; only fig-01 (interfaces & composition) and fig-02 (orchestration) stand on their didactic composite alone, being framework illustrations rather than cellular composition patterns. The baseline composites are toy-real demonstrations — small, illustrative, built to look like the figure and play forward — not fitted models, and every study states that plainly; the scientific-review revision adds `figNN-mechanistic` variants where the behaviour must arise from real coupling. The point is load-bearing but carefully scoped: the paper's figures are not just drawn, they run (H1), and selected figures run on genuine mechanism rather than scripted rules (H2).
question: The meta-modeler's guide argues its case through eleven figures — each a BioRender illustration (panel a) paired with a process-bigraph diagram (panel b) that names the composition behind the biology. Are those diagrams merely drawn, or are they executable? This investigation asks one thing of every figure in the paper: does a runnable process-bigraph composite reproduce, under a behavior-gated test, the exact principle the figure's caption asserts — a process reading and writing typed ports (Fig 1), multi-timescale orchestration (Fig 2), a cellular interface that responds to its inputs (Fig 3), an environment that drives those ports (Fig 4), a viability crossing that swaps the active grain (Fig 5), a molecular mechanism exchanging through typed physical channels (Fig 6), nested hierarchical composites (Fig 7), a cellular interface that emerges from self-maintaining processes (Fig 8), division as a compositional rewrite (Fig 9), cells reorganizing into a collective (Fig 10), and a population evolving toward a selection optimum (Fig 11)? The subject is the figure; the claim is that the paper's diagrams run.
hypothesis:
A TWO-LEVEL hypothesis, with separate verdicts (rewritten per the Oct-2026 scientific review, which asked us to stop conflating structural executability with mechanistic emergence).
H1 (structural executability) — every panel-b diagram in the paper denotes a real, runnable, typed process-bigraph composition: for each of the eleven figures there is a `figNN-runnable` composite that builds through the workspace `build_core`, runs to completion through the engine, and reproduces the caption's stated principle under a behavior-gated test on genuine simulation output. REFUTED IF any figure's composite fails to build/run, or its behavior gate fails, or the readout it reports is not actually produced by the composition (e.g. a value hard-wired rather than computed).
H2 (mechanistic emergence) — SELECTED figures additionally exhibit behaviour that ARISES from mechanistic coupling (shared internal state, conservation, feedback, derived rather than imposed quantities), not solely from imposed rules or a scripted schedule. This is tested only by the `figNN-mechanistic` variants (scientific-review revision), each with counterfactual/ablation controls and quantitative diagnostics. REFUTED FOR A FIGURE IF, under matched-null controls, the claimed behaviour persists when the proposed mechanism is removed (so the behaviour was scripted), or if a conservation/identity the mechanism should enforce fails, or if a quantity presented as derived is in fact an imposed constant.
The two levels get SEPARATE verdicts: H1 is a software/behavioral claim (currently met for all eleven); H2 is a scientific claim met only where a mechanistic variant demonstrates it (in progress — fig-06 and fig-04 established, the rest under revision). The calibrated, spatially-resolved counterparts of these patterns live in the sibling investigation `draft-to-living-cell`.

executive.what_is_this:
The publication figures for the meta-modeler's guide, upgraded from a figure bundle into a full evaluative investigation. Each figure keeps its BioRender illustration (panel a) and its bigraph-loom diagram (panel b) exactly as published, and now carries the executable substance behind that diagram: a runnable `figNN-runnable` process-bigraph composite plus a behavior-gated principle test that demonstrates the figure's caption on genuine simulation output. The organizing claim is that the paper's eleven figures are executable — every panel-b diagram denotes a real composition that runs and reproduces its stated principle, not a hand-drawn schematic. The investigation adds the runnable models, tests, and per-figure verdicts on top of the published panels. (The scientific-review revision additionally adds, for selected figures, a `figNN-mechanistic` variant whose behaviour arises from real coupling rather than imposed rules — see the two-level hypothesis and the per-study variants.)

These are DIDACTIC, TOY-REAL compositions: small, illustrative, built to resemble the figure and play forward, with uncalibrated constants. That is deliberate — the figures are teaching artifacts, and their job is to make the paper's principle legible and playable, not to fit literature. The calibrated, spatially-resolved realizations of the same patterns (a Cellular Potts cell coupled to spatio-flux diffusion and dynamic-FBA, Turing patterns, emergent membranes) live in the sibling investigation `draft-to-living-cell`; seven of the eleven figures name their rigorous cousin there via `parent_studies`. Read this investigation as "the paper's figures execute their captions," and `draft-to-living-cell` as "the paper's patterns hold under calibrated spatial rigor."
executive.verdict:
TWO SEPARATE VERDICTS (the scientific review asked that these not be conflated):
SOFTWARE / STRUCTURAL (H1) — MET for all eleven figures. Every figure carries a runnable `figNN-runnable` composite and a behavior-gated principle test that builds, runs through the engine, and reproduces its caption on genuine simulation output: Fig 1 conserves a transferred quantity to <1e-9; Fig 2 runs two timescales through a shared store; Fig 3's typed ports each respond to their driver; Fig 4's cell senses a gradient and the sense→act loop closes; Fig 5's grain selector flips coarse→fine at the viability crossing; Fig 6's single proton flux drives four typed channels; Fig 7 preserves 6-level containment; Fig 8's coupled processes maintain a bounded pool set; Fig 9 divides one cell into two with DNA conserved; Fig 10 re-parents cells into a biofilm node; Fig 11's mean trait tracks a drifting optimum. All eleven behavior gates pass (verified by the committed test suite; NO independent rerun was performed as part of the scientific review — this verdict rests on the recorded gates, not a fresh re-execution by the reviewer).
SCIENTIFIC / MECHANISTIC (H2) — IN PROGRESS, and varies by figure. Many baseline gates reproduce ENCODED behaviour (regression pins, algebraic/prescribed responses) and cannot by themselves establish biological emergence or causal mechanism. The `figNN-mechanistic` variants supply that evidence where present: fig-06 (torque, efficiency, stall and reversal DERIVED from Δp/ΔG/load; power identity closes; first-principles Δp* threshold predicted and verified) and fig-04 (real cell↔field feedback via a Michaelis–Menten sink carving a diffusing depletion well; mass ledger closes; matched-null controls isolate each arm) are established. The remaining priority figures (5, 8, 10, 11) and the accuracy/compositional figures (2, 3, 9, 1, 7) are under the same upgrade. Until a figure has a passing mechanistic variant with counterfactual controls, its scientific verdict is "executable and self-consistent, mechanism not yet demonstrated" — NOT biological validation, which remains the job of the sibling investigation `draft-to-living-cell`.
decisions_needed: H1 (all figures executable) is met; H2 (mechanistic emergence) is being established variant by variant. Each figure's scientific verdict should be read from its mechanistic variant (where one exists) and its two-layer `conclusion_verdicts`, not from the software-gate pass alone.

Baseline gates that reproduce algebraic or prescribed responses are IMPLEMENTATION VERIFICATION, not mechanistic evidence; where a figure's claim is "emergence" (fig-05/08/09/10/11) the competing programmed-vs-emergent interpretation (see `competing_interpretations`) must be resolved by the mechanistic variant's ablations before any emergence claim stands.

Two figures (fig-01 interfaces & composition, fig-02 orchestration) have no calibrated cousin in `draft-to-living-cell` — they stand on their didactic/mechanistic composite alone by design, being framework illustrations rather than cellular composition patterns. (fig-07 nested hierarchy DOES participate in the spine via its interface dependency; it is not standalone.)

scientific_argument.main_claim: The eleven figures of the meta-modeler's guide are executable artifacts, not just illustrations. Each figure's panel-b process-bigraph diagram denotes a real, registered composition (`figNN-runnable`) that runs through the workspace's own `build_core`, and when it runs it reproduces the principle the figure's caption states — checked by a behavior-gated test, not asserted. The claim is about executability (the diagram is a runnable specification), not biological calibration; the sibling investigation `draft-to-living-cell` carries each pattern to spatially-resolved, controlled rigor.
evidence_for: fig-01 (interfaces & composition) — the paper's definitional figure runs: one typed `StoreTransfer` wired source→sink conserves total amount to 1e-9 at every tick, so the minimal composition the whole guide is built from is itself an executable, conservation-respecting object.

fig-05 (disintegration) — the grain-swap payoff: one shared biomass/energy interface realized at three grains gives biomass 4.0 / 2.67 / 6.29 (coarse / kinetic / real-COBRApy dFBA), and only the FBA grain shows acetate overflow (secretions 30.45 vs 1.6) — the figure's "same interface, different grain" principle, measured off the engine (workbench 0.4.1).

fig-06 (molecular interface) — the F₁Fₒ ATP synthase as one process exposing four typed physical ports (chemical / electrical / mechanical / thermal) from a single proton flux; the driven `fig06-runnable` sweeps the output 20→128 as the proton-motive drive ramps, so the four modalities are one coupled device, not four drawn arrows.

fig-08 (self-organized processes) — the minimal cell, inert on the old engine, now grows across its coupled stores on workbench 0.4.1 (membrane 0.2→1.4, protein pool 0.3→1.57, energy 0.5→0.87), isolated by two process-knockout controls — containment, metabolism, gene expression, replication and diffusion composing into a maintained whole.

fig-09 (growth & division) as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` with exact DNA conservation + equipartition at every division event, and fig-10 / fig-11 (development / evolution) as real runtime structure changes (attachment preserving cell count and biomass; a population tree with standing trait variation) rather than redrawn pictures.
evidence_against: Every `figNN-runnable` composite is didactic and uncalibrated — toy-real constants chosen to make the principle legible in a short run, not fitted to any organism or literature target. A passing gate shows the figure's principle is reproduced on genuine output, not that the biology is quantitatively validated.

fig-11 (evolution) is a structural figure: its executable carries only a `population`/`environment` tree with no scalar time-series, so its evidence is population-tree snapshots, not a dynamics curve.

The bare-draft `fig06-executable` output is flat (chemical_out pinned at the k_cat constant 100.0) — the figure's behavior lives in the driven `fig06-runnable`, so the executability claim rests on the runnable composite plus its driver, not the inert draft alone.

Several figures realize only part of their full biology (two of the four physical interface modalities stay unrealized where they appear); per-study confidence is held at Provisional throughout — the figures execute, but their scientific validation is the sibling investigation's job.
caveats: Executable is not the same as validated: this investigation's claim is narrow — the paper's eleven figures run and reproduce their captions — and deliberately stops short of biological fidelity.
All numbers are from workbench 0.4.1 didactic composites; the prior figure bundle's values predate the engine update and were refreshed where they drifted.

competing_frameworks.prediction: On the illustration view, a paper figure is a drawing: its panel-b diagram documents an idea for a human reader but is not itself a runnable object — you could not press play on the diagram and recover the behavior the caption claims, because the composition it depicts was never executable. This investigation discriminates against that view: every panel-b diagram here is a registered process-bigraph composite that runs through the workspace core and reproduces its figure's stated principle under a behavior-gated test, so the eleven diagrams are executable specifications, not pictures of one.

studies.name: fig-01
studies.title: fig-01: Interfaces & composition
studies.question: Is the paper's definitional Fig 1 (§Interfaces and composition, Fig composition_framework) executable rather than merely drawn -- does the smallest honest process bigraph, one typed process wired through ports to two nested place-graph stores, actually run and move quantity from a source store to a sink store while conserving the total?

findings.statement: The paper's definitional Fig 1 is executable, not merely drawn. The minimal process bigraph -- one typed `StoreTransfer` process wired through a `source` input port and `source`/`sink` output ports to two scalar place-graph stores -- builds and runs forward through the process-bigraph engine, and the wired stores genuinely evolve: source store_a drains from 1.0 to ~0.0388 and sink store_b fills from 0.0 to ~0.9612 over 20 ticks, both strictly monotone. This is the dynamics behind the figure's static signature (a process reading and writing shared variables through ports wired to stores) shown to actually run.

evidence.observed: store_a 1.0 -> 0.03876, store_b 0.0 -> 0.96124 over ticks 0..20, strictly monotone

findings.statement: The transfer conserves quantity exactly, and because it is fixed-rate deterministic the trajectory is exact, not merely directional. store_a + store_b stays fixed at the seeded total 1.0 to round-off at every tick (the two port writes are equal-and-opposite by construction); store_a[n] == 0.85^n and store_b[n] == 1 - 0.85^n to 1e-12 at every tick; and the sink overtakes the source at tick 5. The interface (ports/wiring) carries a conservative transfer, and the whole run reproduces exactly with no seed -- the toy is honest about exactly what it does.

evidence.observed: store_a[n] == 0.85^n, store_b[n] == 1 - 0.85^n to 1e-12; total == 1.0 to 1e-9 every tick; sink overtakes source at tick 5

findings.statement: The fixed-rate transfer has an exact geometric half-life that pins the crossover: the analytic half-life is n½ = ln2 / ln(1/0.85) = 4.265 ticks, so the source first falls to or below half the seeded total (0.5) at tick 5 -- which is exactly the tick at which the sink overtakes the source. The two landmarks (half-drained source, sink/source crossover) coincide because store_b = 1 - store_a, so store_b > store_a precisely when store_a < 0.5. Confirmed in-memory on fig01-runnable (store_a first <= 0.5 at tick 5, value 0.4437 == 0.85^5; interior exactness store_a[10] == 0.85^10 == 0.196874), so the crossover is not a tuned coincidence but a deterministic consequence of the single rate constant.

provenance.analysis_script: in-memory Composite build from fig01-runnable.composite.json + gather_emitter_results (workbench 0.4.1)

findings.statement: The paper's composition point is made measurable: ONE reusable, reversible, typed CompartmentTransport class, REWIRED without any code change, produces different dynamics. On a genuinely nested three-compartment place graph the SAME class on two edges gives a linear chain A↔B↔C that drives quantity out to the deep organelle (equilibrium A:B:C = 1:4:16) and a hub A↔B,A↔C that splits it evenly (1:4:4). Conservation of A+B+C holds to 2.2e-16 in both. Topology lives in the WIRING and controls the outcome — the essence of compositional modelling, shown on the engine rather than drawn.

evidence.observed: chain final A:B:C = 0.049:0.191:0.760 vs hub 0.111:0.444:0.444; total residual 2.2e-16

findings.statement: Types are load-bearing, and the baseline's famous 0.85^n is re-cast honestly. The transport ports are typed `concentration`: core.check accepts a float and REJECTS a structural string, and forcing the incompatible wiring breaks the run — a schema-level negative type-compatibility control. The reversible transport relaxes to its detailed-balance equilibrium (sink/source = k_f/k_r = 4), not a one-way drain. And the exact 0.85^n geometric decay the baseline reported as "novel" is correctly re-labelled: it is the k_reverse→0 limit of this transport (recovered to 5.5e-9) — EQUATION-SPECIFIC solver verification, not a scientific discovery.

evidence.observed: core.check(concentration, string)=False; hub equilibrium ratio 4.0; 0.85^n recovered to 5.5e-9 in the irreversible limit

studies.name: fig-02
studies.title: fig-02: Orchestration
studies.question: Is the paper's orchestration claim (Fig orchestration, panel a) executable rather than merely drawn -- does a runnable process-bigraph composite in which two processes update at DIFFERENT rates through ONE shared store actually reproduce multi-timescale coordination: the fast process filling the shared pool far more often than the slow one converts it, the two rates coordinated through the shared store, and the combined trajectory reflecting both timescales while conserving mass?

findings.statement: The paper's multi-timescale orchestration claim (Fig orchestration, panel a) is executable: two processes updating at different rates through one shared pool store reproduce panel (a) as a runnable, deterministic trajectory. The fast process updates the shared store on every tick (20 changes) while the slow process converts only 3 times, so the fast clock visibly outpaces the slow one; molecules is a sawtooth (rises +1/tick, drawn down at each slow firing t=10, 15, 20) and biomass advances in a coarse monotone staircase on the slow clock (0 -> 3.0 -> 7.2 -> 11.88), so the combined trajectory reflects both timescales at once. All deterministic across repeated runs.

evidence.observed: fast pool 20 changes vs slow store 3 changes; molecules sawtooth; biomass staircase 0 -> 3.0 -> 7.2 -> 11.88

findings.statement: The two rates are coordinated through ONE shared store and mass is conserved across the timescales: the fast process is the sole source and the slow process only moves mass between molecules and biomass within the pool, so at every emitted tick the shared-store total (molecules + biomass) equals the cumulative fast injection, which for rate=1.0 equals the elapsed time exactly -- ending 8.12 + 11.88 = 20.0 at tick 20. Nothing is created or lost in crossing timescales. This is the honest core of "combining updates across timescales": coordination through a shared variable that conserves what it holds. Deterministic -- no RNG.

evidence.observed: molecules + biomass == time at every tick (t=5:5, t=10:10, t=15:15, t=20:20); final split 8.12 + 11.88 == 20.0

findings.statement: The cross-timescale conservation invariant holds at EVERY one of the 21 emitted ticks, not merely at the four sampled slow-firing landmarks: re-run in-memory, molecules + biomass == elapsed time to within 1e-9 for all ticks 0..20 (checked exhaustively, not spot-checked). Each slow firing converts exactly yield_frac (0.6) of the pool sampled at the start of its 5-tick window -- molecules at t=5, 10, 15 are 5.0, 7.0, 7.8, giving biomass increments 0.6x5.0=3.0, 0.6x7.0=4.2, 0.6x7.8=4.68 and the staircase levels [0.0, 3.0, 7.2, 11.88]. The invariant and the increment rule are therefore properties of the composition itself -- one source process plus one mass-moving process on a shared store -- not artifacts of where the series was sampled.

evidence.observed: molecules + biomass == elapsed time for all 21 ticks (exhaustive, to 1e-9); biomass increments 3.0/4.2/4.68 == 0.6 x window-start pool (5.0/7.0/7.8); final split 8.12 + 11.88 == 20.0

provenance.analysis_script: in-memory Composite build from fig02-runnable.composite.json + gather_emitter_results, all-ticks conservation check (workbench 0.4.1)

findings.statement: The baseline's "molecules + biomass == elapsed time" is a CUMULATIVE EXTERNAL-INPUT budget, not closed-system mass conservation — the mechanistic variant makes this explicit and honest. With a genuine first-order turnover routing mass to a waste sink, the full ledger cumulative_input = ΔpoolMetabolite + Δbiomass + Δwaste closes to 1.8e-15 on every step, while pool+biomass reaches only ~2.2 of the 20.0 input (waste carries ~17.8). So the quantity that "equals time" in the baseline is the input, not a conserved internal total; biomass is merely the yield-fraction of throughput.

evidence.observed: ledger residual ≤1.8e-15; final pool+biomass ≈2.2 vs cumulative input 20.0; waste ~17.8

findings.statement: Multirate SCHEDULING and numerical ACCURACY are distinct axes — the baseline conflated them. Refining the whole scheme converges in the stiff metabolite pool with L1 error 2.27→0.011 as Δt halves (~O(Δt), first-order Euler): accuracy is a measurable convergence property. Separately, the pool error is controlled by the FAST clock — a coarse fast clock (r·Δt=1.5) overshoots the quasi-steady pool in the transient while a fine fast clock tracks the reference, independent of the slow clock. That is exactly the value of multirate: a stiff process resolved on its own fast clock stays accurate even while a smooth process uses a coarse clock. The scheduler is also well-posed: swapping the process firing order leaves the trajectory identical (<1e-12), because both read the pool at the tick boundary and return summed, commuting deltas.

evidence.observed: L1 pool error 2.27→0.011 as Δt halves; fast-clock refinement cuts transient error; order-swap identical <1e-12

studies.claim: The paper's multi-timescale orchestration claim (Fig orchestration, panel a) is executable, not merely drawn: composing a fast process and a slow process through ONE shared `pool` store, each updating on its own interval, reproduces panel (a)'s "processes that update at different rates through a shared store" as a runnable, deterministic trajectory. Over a fixed 20-tick run the fast process updates the shared store on every tick (20 changes) while the slow process converts only 3 times, `molecules` is a sawtooth (rises on the fast clock, drawn down at each slow firing), `biomass` advances monotonically in a coarse staircase on the slow clock (levels 0 -> 3.0 -> 7.2 -> 11.88, never returning to the pool), and mass is conserved through the shared store across both timescales -- at every tick `molecules + biomass` equals the cumulative fast injection (== elapsed time), ending 8.12 + 11.88 = 20.0. The combined trajectory reflects both timescales at once; the composite is didactic and uncalibrated, so this demonstrates the ORCHESTRATION MECHANISM, not any biological magnitude.

biological_validation.basis: Reported in two layers, per the review. BEHAVIORAL (baseline fig02-runnable): the multirate signature runs — fast clock outpaces slow (20 vs 3 changes), sawtooth pool, coarse biomass staircase. BUT its "molecules + biomass == elapsed time" is a cumulative-input artefact, not conservation — behavioral verification, and the conservation phrasing was overstated. MECHANISTIC (variant fig02-mechanistic): the honest input-output ledger cumulative_input = ΔM + Δbiomass + Δwaste closes to 1.8e-15 with waste carrying most throughput (invariant); numerical accuracy is a measured O(Δt) convergence of the stiff pool, distinct from scheduling (numerical_convergence + mechanistic_ablation); and the scheduler is order-invariant (invariant). This supplies genuine mechanistic support for the orchestration claim and corrects the conservation overstatement. NOT biological calibration — the rates/intervals are didactic.

No optional heavy dependencies -- the demonstration is a minimal two-process composite.

explanatory_gain.basis: Making Fig orchestration panel (a) runnable -- rather than only drawn -- turns the paper's composition-vs-orchestration distinction into a checked fact: one can point to a live trajectory where two processes provably update at different rates through a shared store, the combined series carries both timescales, and mass is conserved across them. It grounds the paper's central figures-are-executable claim for the orchestration figure.

studies.name: fig-03
studies.title: fig-03: The cellular interface
studies.question: The paper's §Cellular interface (Fig cell_interface) defines a cell as an organization that senses and acts on its environment through typed PORTS -- "each port is a typed connection from the cell to a single variable in the shared state, with a type that fixes the units of what crosses it." Fig cell_interface a. shows interaction modalities as ports (nutrient exchange, motile force, growth, electrical signaling); Fig cell_interface b. shows a minimal interface combining physical exchange ports with higher-level cellular variables (growth, shape, objectives, viability bounds). Is that interface EXECUTABLE rather than merely drawn -- i.e. does a runnable process-bigraph composite exercise those typed ports so that each port's value RESPONDS to its driving environmental input, demonstrating the typed cell -> shared-variable connection the caption asserts?

findings.statement: Fig cell_interface is executable, not merely drawn: composing one bounded cell (`CellularInterfaceHandler`) with a four-driver environment through the `fig03-runnable` composite exercises the caption's typed interface ports so each responds to its driving input. The chemical exchange port and the growth port respond to chemical supply (a 5x supply gives exactly 5x uptake flux and a strictly larger Monod growth rate); the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports each respond linearly to their own driver and read zero when it is off; and the higher-level shape (volume) port accretes strictly (1.0 -> 10.6) as the cell grows. Each is a deterministic typed cell -> shared-variable connection.

studies.name: fig-11
studies.title: fig-11: Evolution
studies.question: Does the paper's §Evolution figure (Fig 11) hold as a runnable place-graph rewrite -- a top-level population of identically-schema'd cells, each exposing a scalar trait, evolving over generations toward a selection optimum set by the environmental niche, so that (Fig 11b) the trait distribution shifts toward the optimum via binary fission + heritable mutation + selection, while division itself (Fig 11a) is a discrete event that REPLACES a parent cell with two daughters?

findings.statement: A `population` of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes coupled to an `environment` niche through one `PopulationEvolution` process reproduces the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11b) as a runnable place-graph rewrite: under Gaussian selection for a drifting optimum, the population mean trait -- starting at 0.0, a gap of 1.0 below the niche optimum -- climbs to ~1.68 and closes the gap to ~0.12 as the optimum drifts from 1.0 to 1.80, the trait distribution shifting toward the environmental optimum via variation (mutation) + heritability + selection. Confirmed (seed=1, deterministic): optimum 1.0 -> 1.80 monotone, mean trait 0.0 -> ~1.68, gap 1.0 -> ~0.12.

evidence.observed: mean trait 0.0 (gap 1.0) -> ~1.68 (gap ~0.12); optimum 1.0 -> 1.80

findings.statement: Division is a genuine place-graph rewrite by binary fission (Fig 11a): a dividing cell is REPLACED by two fresh daughter nodes rather than duplicated in place. Confirmed (seed=1): the founder cell_0 is deleted and replaced by exactly two new nodes (cell_1, cell_2) at the first division; below carrying capacity every topology change adds exactly two daughters per vanished parent (appeared == 2*vanished); the lineage grows to capacity (12) and never exceeds it as death-by-selection culls the least-fit cells; and no retired cell id is ever reused -- each daughter is a genuinely new place-graph vertex.

evidence.observed: cell_0 -> {cell_1, cell_2} at first division; appeared == 2*vanished below capacity; size caps at 12; no id reused

findings.statement: The evolution run is fully deterministic under the pinned seed (seed=1): two independent builds of the composite emit byte-identical (size, mean_trait, optimum) trajectories and identical daughter-node ids. This makes the pinned integers in the behavior tests (final size 12, optimum 1.80) true regression pins rather than run-to-run-variable magnitudes.

evidence.observed: two independent runs produce identical trajectories and daughter ids

findings.statement: Reading the population tree's node contents at successive snapshots shows two structural features beyond the mean-trait track: standing variation and adaptation lag. (1) The final-generation snapshot is a trait CLOUD with width, not a converged point -- its 12 cell nodes span traits 1.47 to 1.91 (range 0.44, population standard deviation 0.131) around the optimum 1.80, because the Gaussian mutation injected at each binary fission keeps replenishing heritable variation that selection then shapes. (2) The population LAGS the moving target: the derived mean-trait gap to the drifting optimum closes below 0.4 only at generation 22 (from an initial gap of 1.0) and is still 0.12 at generation 40 -- the cloud chases but never catches the continuously drifting optimum, the signature of adaptation lag. Both are read from the per-generation population snapshots; confirmed in-memory (seed=1, deterministic).

evidence.observed: final snapshot (12 cells): traits min 1.470 / max 1.910 / range 0.440 / pop std 0.131 about optimum 1.80; derived mean-gap first < 0.4 at generation 22, gap 0.12 at generation 40

findings.statement: The §Evolution (Fig 11) adaptation claim is made QUANTITATIVE and distinguished from drift, over many seeds. In a real Wright–Fisher population (N=300), viability selection tracks the drifting optimum with a small bounded lag (0.39±0.04 over 40 seeds), while the matched NEUTRAL control (selection off) drifts away to a lag of 2.38±0.23 — a separation far larger than the across-seed spread. The realized heritability (parent–offspring regression) is 0.998, so the response obeys the breeder's equation R = h²·S, and a no-mutation control shows the variance eroding (0.21 → 0.001) when the source of variation is removed. This directly answers the review's point that the baseline's single-seed mean "tracking an imposed optimum" was expected by design: here the tracking is a statistical, controlled, heritability-grounded result.

evidence.observed: selection lag 0.39±0.04 vs neutral 2.38±0.23 (40 seeds); h²=0.998; no-mutation variance 0.21→0.001

findings.statement: A first-principles failure prediction is stated and passes: because the per-generation response is bounded (R = h²·S, limited by standing variance), the tracking lag must grow with the optimum's drift rate and run away once drift exceeds what selection can supply (an adaptation-failure / evolutionary-rescue threshold). A 20-seed drift sweep confirms the lag rising monotonically 0.11 → 11.2 as drift rises 0.02 → 0.55. Honest caveats, per the review: the mean trait moving toward the optimum is EXPECTED BY DESIGN — the content is the quantitative conditions (heritability, mutation supply, drift rate) under which adaptation succeeds or fails, the stochastic spread across seeds, and the explicit failure regime. At the baseline's small N=12 the across-seed drift is large; this variant uses N=300 and many replicates precisely to separate signal from drift.

evidence.observed: final lag 0.11 (drift 0.02) → 11.2 (drift 0.55), monotone runaway; single-seed = reproducibility only

findings.statement: Fitness can be DERIVED from an executable metabolic trait rather than prescribed. In the uptake mode each individual's trait is an uptake investment a; growth is a saturating Michaelis–Menten uptake of a drifting resource minus a quadratic cost, g(a) = Vmax·a·R/(Km+a) − cost·a², whose interior optimum a* drifts endogenously with the resource. The evolved mean trait climbs and tracks a* at correlation > 0.95 — the moving target is a consequence of a metabolic tradeoff, not an imposed Gaussian. Honest limits: still a single-locus asexual clonal model (no genome, recombination, epistasis), overdamped selection, and didactic rate constants; the quantitative lag in the uptake mode reflects a fast resource drift relative to the mutational supply.

evidence.observed: evolved mean tracks derived a* at corr > 0.95 over 50 generations (25 seeds)
